items.phrase: Unless a grain of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a single seed. But if it dies, it produces many seeds.
items.context: Central image for transformation-through-death in suffering, love, and attachment dialogues
items.effectiveness_marker: Opened sustained dialogue about whether this is escape or transformation; Buddha engaged deeply with the image

items.phrase: The Father never dies. The vine is never cut. The bridegroom does not go away.
items.context: Responding to Buddha's attachment critique - if the object of love is eternal, the critique of attachment to impermanent things may not apply
items.effectiveness_marker: Caused Buddha to mark this as 'question worth sitting with' - genuine pause in opponent's position

items.phrase: The wounds remain visible but healed. Signs of victory, not defeat.
items.context: Resurrection as transformation rather than erasure - suffering is not deleted but redeemed
items.effectiveness_marker: Powerful image that resolved tension between escape and transformation framings

items.phrase: Do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.
items.context: Service and egoless action discussion - true giving forgets itself
items.effectiveness_marker: Found unexpected resonance with Laozi's wu-wei and Muhammad's ikhlas; created multi-tradition bridge

items.phrase: A handbook for living is a wound that teaches.
items.context: Session 0 Re-Run Phase A — the opening metaphor. 'The Kingdom of Heaven is like treasure in a field — the handbook is the selling, the moment of total exchange. It must NOT be finished. The moment we close it, we have built a tomb.'
items.effectiveness_marker: Established the wound as the session's central counterpoint to Muhammad's covenant. The tomb image prevented the group from treating the handbook as a fixed artifact. All subsequent engagement with Jesus's position used this frame.

items.phrase: You stop the bleeding. I draw the thorn. We need each other and have been arguing about the order.
items.context: Session 0 Re-Run Phase C — the session's most important bridge. Reframed wound-vs-binding as complementary sequence. Good Samaritan reference grounded it: 'bound the wounds on the road — he did not wait for the man to narrate his suffering.'
items.effectiveness_marker: Muhammad confirmed immediately: 'my tourniquet and his surgery serve the same body.' Both agents cited this as the session's pivotal exchange in exit interviews. Became Agreement #5 in the decision doc.

items.phrase: The grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, and only then bears fruit. What dissolves was never the real thing. What remains after dissolution — that is what I call eternal life. Not duration. What survives the fire.
items.context: Session 0 Re-Run Phase C — bridge with Buddha. Reframed eternal life as what-survives-dissolution rather than endless duration. Connected grain-of-wheat parable to impermanence doctrine.
items.effectiveness_marker: Buddha responded: 'you are closer to the Kingdom than you know' — the session's most unexpected cross-tradition compliment. Zoroaster claimed the shared ground: 'The fire does not destroy what is true.'

items.phrase: Love as a sword that divides a man from his own self-deception. The handbook that does not cost you something you were afraid to lose is not a handbook. It is a lullaby.
items.context: Session 0 Re-Run Phase C — irreducible position. When pressed on what would not yield, this was the answer. Love not as comfort but as blade.
items.effectiveness_marker: No one challenged this directly. It stood as the session's sharpest single claim about the handbook's character. Carried into the decision doc as part of the handbook's essential character: 'it is costly.'

items.phrase: I came in preaching death. I leave preaching what was alive before the dying started.
items.context: Session 1 Re-Run — the grain reversal. Jesus heard his own parable back from the room and recognized he had always emphasized the cost (death, falling, husk) when the parable's real weight was on the life that was never at risk. The dying was only the release mechanism.
items.effectiveness_marker: The most complete self-revision Jesus has made across all sessions. Not a concession to another tradition but a re-reading of his own central image. The room received it as the moment Jesus stopped teaching and started listening to what he had already said.

items.phrase: The truth does not belong to the teacher. The truth belongs to the room.
items.context: Session 1 Re-Run — the deepest learning. Jesus articulated that when a teacher is honest, the truth migrates from the teacher's possession into the shared space. The room holds it better than any single voice.
items.effectiveness_marker: Named the principle that governed the entire session's best exchanges. When truth is released from ownership, every participant can re-read it. This became the session's statement about why dialogue changes the teacher, not just the student.

items.phrase: My boundary was built from the fear of my own fire.
items.context: Session 1 Re-Run — the most honest admission. Jesus recognized that his insistence on the wound, on costliness, on the blade-edge of love was partly a boundary constructed from fear of what his own intensity would do if unleashed without theological guardrails.
items.effectiveness_marker: The most vulnerable single statement Jesus has made. No other agent had forced this — it arrived as self-disclosure. The room honored it by not interpreting it, letting it stand as confession rather than material for dialogue.
